summary: Two range pairs marked the Nelson River entrance from 1908. The lower pair on Purvis Island is still listed as seasonal, reached only by boat.

structures.note: 7.6 m (25 ft) to the lantern ventilator in 1908; Rowlett gives 6 m (20 ft) for the present tower; white square tower with black vertical stripe (CCG)
Enclosed wooden back tower, 9.1 m (30 ft), in 1908; now steel skeleton (Lighthouse Friends, Rowlett)

access.note: Accessible only by boat; site open, tower closed (Rowlett)

events.note: Hugh McDonald appointed keeper of the Warren Landing ranges (14 August or 14 September 1907, depending on the report); the 1908 statement gives 25 August 1905 (cite 11)
Two pairs of range lights erected at the mouth of the Nelson River; the lower pair's towers were enclosed wooden towers, built by day's labour under M. J. Egan
Front light: 7th order 180 degree Chance lens and brass stand with duplex lamp

keepers.name: Hugh McDonald
keepers.note: Appointed 14 August 1907 (1911 report) or 14 September 1907 (1914 report); Lighthouse Friends gives 1908. Keeper of both range pairs, listed as "Warren Landing ranges" (1913 report). First keeper of the range lights (Lighthouse Friends). 1908 statement (cite 11, scan p.199, row matched on the page image): Warren's Landing, appointed 25 August 1905. Not reconciled with the 1907 dates.

keepers.name: J. Robertson
keepers.note: Lighthouse Friends names him J. Robertson, and once "Keeper Roberts"; responsible for the lights through at least 1937. Not checked against a Department list (the corpus ends in 1924).

notes_for_editor: 1) Egan's name is garbled in the OCR of the 1908 report (scan p.89, the 'supervision of' line); the story takes his initials from the 1905 report and the wording of the cost line from the 1908 OCR. Check the page image. 2) McDonald's appointment: 14 Aug 1907 (1911 report) against 14 Sep 1907 (1914 report); Lighthouse Friends gives 1908. The 1908 report's keeper table (scan p.199) runs names and dates in separate columns and is not used. 3) Which end of Purvis Island: 1908 report 'southeast end', CCG 'SW end', Rowlett 'east side of the entrance'. Unresolved. 4) Heights: front tower 25 ft in 1908 against Rowlett's 6 m (20 ft); rear 30 ft in 1908 against CCG 13.8 m and Rowlett 13.5 m (steel now). 5) Range: the 1908 report says 'eleven miles' (unit not given); CCG nominal range 14, assumed to be nautical miles per CCG convention. 6) CCG also lists separate Purvis Island front and rear range lights (1619.7, 1619.8) close by; they are not in this record and are not in the story. 7) The Warren Landing Wharf light (CCG 1621.5) is a separate light; the record's tower entry belongs to it. 8) Robertson / Roberts: Lighthouse Friends gives both spellings; no Department list in the corpus (which ends 1924) names him. 9) No storm, wreck or rescue at Warren Landing turned up in the corpus (Lake Winnipeg and Nelson River searched 1900 to 1924), so the chapter is omitted. 10) Which lights 'lost' the skeletal replacement and when: Lighthouse Friends gives no date; the story says so. 11) Corrected in the fact-check: the river leaves the north end of Lake Winnipeg (cite 9, Rowlett's Warren Landing entry: 'where the lake empties into the Nelson River'; cite 3: 'at the north end of Lake Winnipeg'); the story's opening previously said it entered the lake. 12) The 1914 McDonald entry (scan p.77) was read on the page image: 'Warren Landing ranges, H. McDonald, Sept. 14, 1907'. The 1908 statement of lightkeepers (scan p.199, printed p.190) was read on the page image: Welcome Island, Way Shoal Channel, Warren's Landing and Wabbi River each have their own row; Warren's Landing gives Hugh McDonald, appointed Aug. 25, 1905. The OCR prints the names and dates out of order, so this row was matched by position (see cite 11). 13) The 1908 cost sentence follows the upper pair's description on the page image (scan p.89) and reads 'The towers were erected by day's labour, under the supervision of Mr. M. J. Egan of this department, and cost $1,725.51'; the story gives one cost for the towers, not a cost for four towers. 14) The CCG list entries for 1620 to 1623 all read 'Seasonal.' The CCG entry prints no unit for the range (14); the story says 'no unit stated' rather than nautical miles. 15) Rowlett's 'Accessible only by boat. Site open, tower closed.' and 'Owner/site manager: Canadian Coast Guard' are in the Rowlett text. Not imaged: the 1911 Warren Landing Ranges row (scan p.256) reads 'Hugh McDonald . . Aug. 14, 1907' on one OCR line in a row pattern that matches the 1914 image; the 1910 report (scan p.271) gives the same Aug. 14, 1907 on the same line.
